stories.headline: ALCS Game 2: Lineups, live updates from Guardians-Rays
stories.summary: The Guardians kept on rolling Monday, winning the ALCS opener over Tampa Bay. Can they take a 2-0 lead Tuesday?
stories.body:
The Cleveland Guardians are rolling.

After dropping the first two games of the American League Division Series, they bounced back to beat the Chicago White Sox three straight times to advance to the next round. In Game 1 of the AL Championship Series on Monday, Cleveland stayed hot, defeating the top-seeded Tampa Bay Rays in comeback fashion.

On Tuesday, the Guardians will try to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the ALCS. Can they head back to Cleveland for Game 3 just two wins away from a World Series appearance?

Stay tuned for lineups, game action and postgame analysis from St. Petersburg.

stories.headline: North Melbourne knows Blakey's price. The full cost remains unknown
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have made an extraordinary investment in dashing defender Nick Blakey. But the reputational implications remain difficult to quantify, writes Jane Aubrey.
stories.body:
North Melbourne has finally landed its big fish.

After years of trying to attract established stars, the Kangaroos have secured one of the AFL's most exciting defenders on a reported eight-year deal worth more than $11 million.

Nick Blakey is 26, an All-Australian and a player capable of transforming North Melbourne's ball movement. His father, John, won two premierships at Arden Street. There is a certain romance to the homecoming.

But this is no ordinary trade.

Blakey was among five Sydney players suspended for breaching the Swans' behavioural standards following an incident at Melbourne's Pullman Hotel in August. Those club sanctions were separate from an ongoing Victoria Police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the hotel. No charges have been laid, and the disciplinary breaches should not be taken as evidence of criminal wrongdoing by Blakey.

The fallout contributed to his departure despite five years remaining on his contract. Blakey has apologised for the circumstances surrounding his exit and acknowledged the need to rebuild trust.

There is nothing inherently wrong with a second chance. But in professional sport, second chances are rarely distributed independently of talent.

Exceptional talent can change an organisation's appetite for risk.

Consider the contrast between the two clubs.

Sydney developed Blakey through its academy. He became an All-Australian, a life member and a veteran of 173 games and two Grand Finals.

Yet its farewell announcement focused largely on the draft assets received. The Swans acknowledged his contribution, but the emphasis was on what Sydney gained rather than what it lost.

At North Melbourne, the same transaction was cause for celebration.

Two clubs. The same player. Two very different calculations about what comes next.

I previously wrote for ESPN about the Swans' celebrated Bloods culture and the gap between a club's reputation and the standards it actually upholds.

Blakey's move raises a different question: what happens when reputational uncertainty becomes an opportunity for another organisation?

Sydney has secured a substantial draft return and an opportunity to move beyond a fractured relationship. That doesn't mean its decision was purely about principle. Blakey requested the move, and the compensation was significant.

For North Melbourne, the football argument is obvious. But would a player of Blakey's calibre, with five years remaining on his contract, have been available under different circumstances?

The uncertainty surrounding his departure may have created an opportunity North Melbourne would otherwise have struggled to secure.

The club says it has conducted its due diligence. Head of football Brady Rawlings has expressed confidence in the decision but declined to elaborate publicly on the assurances received from Blakey.

There may be legitimate reasons for that confidentiality. But there is a distinction between having confidence in a decision and asking everyone else to share it.

And that brings us to the price North Melbourne has agreed to pay.

Eight years. Reportedly around $11 million. Significant draft capital.

Those costs are measurable. What cannot yet be determined is whether the unresolved Pullman Hotel investigation will have additional reputational or commercial implications for North Melbourne, let alone what those might cost.

The investigation's existence does not establish wrongdoing by Blakey. There may be no additional cost.

But North Melbourne has made a long-term commitment before the broader situation has been resolved.

The club has experience managing uncertainty involving high-profile figures.

When Alastair Clarkson was appointed in August 2022, historical racism allegations relating to his time at Hawthorn had not yet become public. After initially delaying his commencement, North allowed Clarkson to begin coaching while the AFL investigation remained unresolved.

Clarkson denied wrongdoing. The AFL investigation concluded without adverse findings against him, although he took leave during 2023, requiring alternative coaching arrangements.

The club's handling of Tarryn Thomas provides another reference point.

In February 2024, the AFL found Thomas had engaged in multiple acts of misconduct involving women and imposed an 18-match suspension. North Melbourne terminated his contract.

The circumstances are materially different from Blakey's, against whom there has been no comparable AFL misconduct finding. But these episodes raise questions about what North has learned about risk, accountability and organisational standards.

Those questions extend beyond the men's football department.

North Melbourne's reputation belongs to its members, sponsors, staff and an extraordinarily successful AFLW program.

Chief executive Jen Watt reportedly spoke with the women's program about Blakey's recruitment, providing an opportunity for questions.

Consultation is important. But consultation is not necessarily endorsement, nor should women within a sporting organisation be expected to validate decisions about male footballers.

The responsibility rests with those making the decision.

If Blakey plays another 150 games and helps return North Melbourne to September, the trade may be celebrated as a success.

But football success cannot retrospectively answer every question about governance or accountability.

Accepting reputational uncertainty is not inherently poor judgment. Organisations routinely make decisions without knowing every possible outcome.

The measure is whether they understand the risks, take responsibility for them and apply their standards consistently, even when doing so is inconvenient.

North Melbourne has invested heavily in Blakey's ability to transform its football fortunes.

The return will be measured in games, wins, and perhaps premierships.

North Melbourne knows what it has paid for Nick Blakey. Whether there will be a greater cost, and when or how it might emerge, remains unknown.

stories.headline: Panthers RT Moton coughed up blood before clot diagnosis
stories.summary: Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton, 32, told reporters Tuesday that he coughed up blood before being diagnosed with multiple blood clots in June, an ailment that sidelined him through training camp and into the second month of the regular season.
stories.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton said Tuesday that he coughed up blood before being diagnosed with multiple blood clots in late June. The ailment sidelined him throughout training camp and preseason, and well into the second month of the regular season.

Moton, the longest tenured nonspecialist in Carolina, participated in his first padded practice of 2026 on Tuesday after the Panthers activated his 21-day practice window on the non-football injury (NFI) list. Moton's early season stand-in, first-round pick Monroe Freeling, worked with a trainer off to the side because of a knee injury.

Following practice, during his first conversation with reporters since OTAs, Moton detailed his illness and the steps he took to get back onto the field. Moton said upon returning from a youth football camp in Lansing, Michigan, he experienced symptoms that would eventually lead to the discovery of multiple blood clots in his right lung.

"I started coughing up blood -- and it was like a lot of it," Moton said. "And I could start feeling it leaking through my chest even -- something like really different. So, after 15-or-something minutes, I was like 'Yeah, I've got to go to the hospital.' Went to the hospital, they were doing CT scans, ultrasounds, trying to find what was going on. And that's when they found a multitude of clots in my right lung. ... So from there, they put me on blood thinners, and other than that I was just working. I just couldn't have contact on the blood thinners cause having contact on blood thinners can lead to like a brain bleed ... but ultimately doing everything I could to just work and simulate football without the contact up until then."

Moton said he felt as if his chest were congested, but he soon realized the discomfort was more than just typical congestion when he started tasting blood in his mouth. Moton said doctors aren't sure what caused the ailment, but the 32-year-old lineman is more concerned about future prevention. He was told staying hydrated is part of that prevention, as well as moving around when he travels.

Moton has traveled with the team only once this year, as he went to Jacksonville, Florida, for the Panthers' training camp joint practice and preseason game against the Jaguars. He has been consulting with a bloodwork specialist to be prepared for the weeks ahead, including Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles in Philadelphia.

Moton said he was grateful to get back to work on the practice field with his teammates. He had to weigh the risk-reward factor of such a move earlier this summer.

"Ultimately, I had to just weigh the pros and cons of getting off the blood thinners, and then being able to play ball and the chance of it happening [again]," Moton said. "The chances [of a recurrence] are relatively low right now, after being on the blood thinners for three months."

Moton's former Panthers teammate, defensive end DJ Wonnum -- who now plays for the Detroit Lions -- dealt with a blood clot during his first year with Carolina in 2024. Moton said he spoke with Wonnum about their situations.

The veteran tackle said he has been off the thinners for a "couple of weeks now." He noted that he had to wait for his blood to regulate before returning to workouts through the bye week.

Moton, who dealt with notably high blood pressure and lightheadedness before receiving blood thinner treatment, said the ordeal has given him a better appreciation for football and life.

"Honestly, it gave me more gratitude for life in general," Moton said.

The Panthers didn't release an official injury report Tuesday, but Moton donned full pads for the workout. With Freeling dealing with a knee injury, Moton's long-awaited return would be welcomed, if not necessary, to add stability to the line and the offense.

He's getting ready as if his regular-season debut will take place this weekend at Lincoln Financial Field.

"I'm going into it preparing to play," Moton said. "But ultimately, whether I do or not, that's not my decision. That's the higher-ups, right? So, I'm just doing everything I can to prepare as if I'm going in playing."

Along with Moton, defensive end Tershawn Wharton (neck) and running back Trevor Etienne (ankle) had their 21-day practice windows opened on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list and injured reserve, respectively. Like Moton, Wharton has been sidelined since the start of training camp. Etienne sustained his injury in the preseason finale in August.

All three players will have three weeks to be added to the 53-man roster. The Panthers have three open spots on their main depth chart after putting nose tackle Cam Jackson (shoulder) on injured reserve Tuesday.

Jackson is set to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery, according to coach Dave Canales.

stories.headline: Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern
stories.summary: Arsenal's substitutes made the difference once again, but Mikel Arteta's side still have questions as tougher tests await.
stories.body:
LONDON -- If Arsenal's starters don't get you, the finishers probably will.

Lille were firmly in Tuesday's UEFA Champions League game for an hour or so and then a three-goal blitz in seven minutes settled things emphatically.

There were similarities here to last weekend's 2-1 win in the Premier League over Leeds United. The visitors were the better side, but Arteta made a triple substitution shortly after Arsenal took the lead, and his team went on to win.

Lille were not as front-footed as Leeds, but they carried a threat on the break and Arsenal were struggling to break them down until Jurriën Timber marked his first home start since March with a clever touch in the box to free himself and dink a delightful finish over Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer from a tight angle.

Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz were already stripped and ready to come on. Arteta could have thought twice about making the changes given the deadlock was broken, but he went through with it anyway.

"I'm going to do it more now," he joked afterward.

"I felt it was the right moment to do it, the way the game was panning out, the way the opponent was behaving as well, that we needed in those moments, in those spaces, different kinds of players, but that's it.

"Credit to the staff and obviously the ones that come in to create those moments."

"Is it about momentum as well? Yes, it is," he continued. The combination of the dam bursting and the fresh legs overwhelmed the Ligue 1 side to win 3-0.

Timber won the ball back before Ødegaard and Saka combined for Eberechi Eze to side foot the ball home for his first goal of the season. Ødegaard then found Havertz, who demonstrated his game intelligence in recognizing nobody was in a central position as he burst towards the byline, instead cutting it back for Saka to score his 19th European goal for Arsenal, more than anyone else for the club aside from Thierry Henry (42).

The Gunners continue their perfect start to the group stage ahead of next week's testing trip to Bayern Munich, where they will likely need to start better than they have done of late to ensure that record continues.

Nobody can argue with the end product -- that's nine wins from 10 matches this season including August's Community Shield victory over Manchester City -- but if there is an issue to be found, it is perhaps in the need for those "finishers" -- Arteta's preferred moniker for substitutes -- to be so decisive.

He made five changes here, including Viktor Gyökeres leading the line instead of Havertz, with Mikel Merino operating as a No. 10 in place of Ødegaard. Noni Madueke switched to the right to replace Saka, with Eze on the left in a remodeled front four.

The results were inconclusive. Lille combined diligent defending with energetic counterattacking to cause Arsenal problems, most obviously when Ayase Ueda beat David Raya from inside the box, but his goal was disallowed for a tight offside call.

Gyökeres registered just 12 touches, completed six passes from eight attempts and no shots. He was a 65th-minute departure for Havertz, and no player on either team had been involved in the game less.

Arsenal possess tremendous depth all over the pitch -- their "second-choice" back four when everybody is fit, Ben White, Ezri Konsa, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapié, is an embarrassment of riches -- but the drop in the No. 9 position remains a concern.

Havertz is integral in and out of possession for Arsenal, but it also remains true that Arteta felt they needed an upgrade in that position in 2025, which triggered the pursuit of Gyökeres in the first place.

They also were hopeful of luring Julián Álvarez from Atlético Madrid this summer, but after that possibility disappeared, they opted to rely on Havertz, Gyökeres and Merino, whose emergence as a potent goal scorer for Arsenal and Spain is one of the biggest surprises of the past year or more.

It might be enough to win the club's first Champions League. They were penalty kicks away from achieving that feat with that trio last season. But there is frankly more encouragement elsewhere, with Timber looking a threat throughout and reminding everyone of the dynamic dimension he provides from the right.

Eze's evening was more mixed, but his goal was of high quality and a step towards seizing the opportunity of regular game time afforded to him by Christos Tzolis' muscular injury.

Whatever grumbles there are, Arsenal's bandwagon rolls on. That's 14 consecutive Champions League group stage wins now on a night when the club mourned the passing of life president Ken Friar, aged 92.

"There are people in football clubs that they have a role and they fulfill a role," Arteta said.

"And there are other people that they create an identity, they create values and they have a vision to create a future for the football club.

"And I think the legacy that Ken is going to leave to all of us, to our football club and everybody that has been close to him is going to be forever."

Next is Sunday's trip to Nottingham Forest. Arteta will likely shuffle the pack again, but at the moment, one way or another, the right number keeps coming up.

stories.headline: Dream's Gray has minor procedure on hand ahead of Finals opener
stories.summary: Allisha Gray, who has missed the Dream's past two playoff games because of a left hand injury, is still day-to-day heading into the WNBA Finals after undergoing a minor procedure.
stories.body:
Four-time All-Star Allisha Gray underwent a minor procedure on her left hand and is still considered day-to-day for the Atlanta Dream heading into the WNBA Finals, she said Tuesday.

"Progress is great," Gray told WSB-TV when asked at practice whether she'd play in Game 1. "As of right now just day-to-day, and you'll see."

Gray did not clarify whether she had surgery on her hand, and the team declined to say when the procedure occurred.

She was seen taking shots at practice Tuesday, a day before the team travels to the Bay Area for Saturday's Finals opener against No. 2 seed Golden State.

Gray, the top scorer for the No. 4 seed Dream, has missed the past two playoff games after injuring the hand in the first half of Game 1 in a semifinal series against the New York Liberty. She was listed as questionable heading into Game 3 last Friday against New York and went through warmups before being ruled out "in the interest of caution," according to coach Karl Smesko.

The Dream advanced to the Finals with a three-game sweep.

Gray, a 6-foot guard out of South Carolina, averaged 19.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 steals this year while appearing in all 44 regular-season games. She was also the Dream's top scorer (22.0 points per game) during their first-round sweep of the No. 5 seed Washington Mystics.

The Dream and Valkyries will both be competing for their first WNBA championship.

stories.headline: Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'
stories.summary: Don Garber has addressed his September confrontation with Lionel Messi, and the MLS commissioner said he admired the exchange.
stories.body:
Don Garber has addressed his confrontation with Lionel Messi following Inter Miami CF Campeones Cup victory over Cruz Azul in September, with the MLS commissioner saying he admired the exchange.

Following the Campeones Cup victory, Messi and Garber could be seen having a heated discussion before the Inter Miami captain went to celebrate the victory with the rest of his team and family members.

"You know, the best players in the world have passion," Garber said in an interview with Front Office Sports on Tuesday. "The legendary players have more than passion. Leo played on Saturday, scored a couple goals and assists coming out of an international window where he played for Argentina, 39 years old. He's leading our rush for Golden Boot. He's leading our MVP race.

"There are players throughout history, Muhammad Ali, Wayne Gretzky, Michael Jordan who play with a sense of intensity and passion that makes them unique and special, and makes him the GOAT of all GOATS. What is going on there is between me and Leo [Messi], it's not something I am going to talk about with you.

"But I admire it, I appreciate it and I think it's what makes Leo Messi the greatest player ever to play football. And I will say, [he's] the greatest athlete of all time."

Inter Miami beat Cruz Azul 2-0 in the Campeones Cup final with a goal from Messi in the 24th minute before he provided the assist to Casemiro for the second goal. Messi currently has 23 goals and 13 assists in MLS, leading the 2026 Golden Boot race and sitting in second place for most assists so far this regular season.

It's not the first time that Garber and Messi haven't seen eye to eye. In 2025, Garber made a joke about Messi not wanting to talk to him following the decision to suspend him and former teammate Jordi Alba for missing the 2025 MLS All-Star Game.

"I don't think he wants to talk to me," Garber said in 2025. "I didn't treat him like any other player in that decision. So, I probably won't be going to Miami any time soon or hanging out and doing any media work with Leo."

Garber later defended his decision to suspend the two players.

"If you don't do that, you're not gonna be able to lead," Garber said. "You're not gonna be able to command the respect of the ownership. The media is going to s--- on you no matter what. You guys will write a story 'how could you suspend Leo Messi?' after we suspended him, and before we suspended him say 'how could you not?'

"So, the media is irrelevant to that equation. They're gonna hate you all the time."

Garber and Messi later interacted at the 2025 MLS Cup, when the MLS commissioner presented the Inter Miami captain with the trophy. Inter Miami currently sits second place on the Eastern Conference table with 49 points from 28 games.

stories.headline: Brendan Allen submits his case for moving up in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Brendan Allen fought a back-and-forth battle with Christian Leroy Duncan in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event. Going into the fifth round of the meeting of top-10 middleweights, Allen was narrowly ahead on all three scorecards. Of course, he did not know what the judges were thinking.

So Allen took it out of the judges' hands in Round 5, getting Duncan to the ground and efficiently finishing the gritty fight with a rear-naked choke.

With his fourth straight victory, Allen moves up one spot to No. 5 in the ESPN divisional rankings, continuing his recent climb in the middleweight top 10.

That's the only rankings change this week. Duncan remains No. 10 at 185 pounds, and sixth-ranked strawweight Loopy Godínez, who beat unranked Ketlen Souza by decision on Saturday's undercard, also retains her spot.

Here are the ESPN pound-for-pound MMA rankings and a list of current UFC champions in all weight classes.

Results are current; rankings as of Oct. 13. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

stories.headline: Christian Horner: Mercedes' Toto Wolff has it 'easy' at the moment
stories.summary: Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.
stories.body:
Former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner has suggested that Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has "got it quite easy" at the moment.

Horner, 52, officially left Red Bull Racing in September last year having been relieved of "operational duties" following last July's British Grand Prix. It ended a 20-year career with the team, where he won eight drivers' and six constructors' titles.

The past decade saw Horner spar with Wolff as Red Bull and Mercedes did battle.

This season, Horner's old team are currently fourth in the constructors' standings with 11 podiums and two wins, both claimed by Max Verstappen during this month's races in Bahrain and Singapore.

Mercedes top the constructors' leaderboard, while Kimi Antonelli is first in the drivers' standings having won eight races so far.

A potential return to F1 for Horner remains a hot topic and in an interview earlier this year, Wolff suggested Horner had "broken a lot of glass."

In an interview with the Guardian, Horner said: "He [Wolff] also said this [Red Bull] engine was going to be completely s--t and a disaster.

"Toto's got it quite easy at the moment. Zak Brown [head of McLaren] is compromised because he's using Toto's engine so he can't ruffle feathers.

"All sport needs rivalry, whether it's [Alex] Ferguson and [Arsene] Wenger, [Jose] Mourinho and (Pep) Guardiola. It percolates and polarises. I used that to galvanise good people to take on Mercedes."

- Formula 1 to return to Africa in 'early 2030s' as Rwanda race confirmed

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Toto Wolff finds quirky solution to Kimi Antonelli track limits 'stress'

Horner also revealed in the interview that he has suffered from panic attacks and has worked to recognise the symptoms.

"I didn't know what it was. You suddenly feel dizzy and conscious of your breathing and you think there's something strange going on. I put it down to having had too much coffee on an oppressive, muggy, thundery day," he said.

"Then it happened again. I got checked out and there was nothing physically the matter. They said: 'We think you have anxiety. Your breathing's very shallow.' It was my body telling me you're pushing pretty hard here. I'm able to recognise the symptoms now and let it go, and breathe."

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Suter, Neighbours and McTavish score 2 each as the Blues rout the Senators 7-2
stories.summary: — Pius Suter, Jake Neighbours and Mason McTavish each had a pair of goals to lead the St. Louis Blues to a 7-2 win over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night.
stories.body:
OTTAWA, Ontario -- — Pius Suter, Jake Neighbours and Mason McTavish each had a pair of goals to lead the St. Louis Blues to a 7-2 win over the Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night.


Adam Jiricek also scored for the Blues, Pavel Buchnevich had three assists and Joel Hofer stopped 15 shots.


Claude Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund scored for the Senators, whose three game win streak came to an end. Samuel Ersson, making his second start for Ottawa, made 19 saves.


Ottawa was playing the second game of a back-to-back, coming off a 4-1 win against the New Jersey Devils on Monday.


The Blues took a 4-1 lead midway through the third when Suter beat Ersson short side from a sharp angle. Neighbours scored his second off a snap shot, McTavish scored on the power play, and Jiricek scored his first career goal to round out the scoring.


Zetterlund added a late power-play goal to make it 7-2.


St. Louis took a 2-0 lead midway through the second when Neighbours stepped in with a shot from the top of the slot and wristed a shot through traffic to beat Ersson glove side.


Giroux cut the lead in half with 2:08 remaining in the second on a feed from Tim Stutzle, but the Blues responded 33 seconds later. Some poor defensive zone coverage allowed McTavish to get a shot past Ersson from the top of the crease.


The Blues opened the scoring at 14:28 of the first period with a short-handed goal. Colton Parayko won a battle along the boards and found Suter with some open space and he beat Ersson blocker side.


With his second-period goal, Giroux recorded his 1,170th career point, tying Bobby Hull for 59th on the NHL’s career scoring list.


Up next
Blues: At Minnesota on Thursday.


Senators: Host the New York Islanders on Thursday.

stories.headline: Shohei Ohtani will be in Dodgers' Game 3 NLCS lineup, Dave Roberts says
stories.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters Tuesday that struggling superstar Shohei Ohtani will be in the lineup for Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday vs. the Milwaukee Brewers.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Shohei Ohtani was "convicted" and "adamant" that he is close to recovering from his prodigious slump and will be in the lineup for Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday night, Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before his team's workout Tuesday afternoon.

Ohtani went 0-for-4 with two strikeouts in the Dodgers' 7-4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Monday, one that put his team in a 2-0 hole in the best-of-seven NLCS. Roberts planned to check with his two-way superstar when the team returned to Los Angeles to gauge whether he would continue playing, but a source told ESPN that Ohtani would remain in the lineup as long as he deemed himself healthy enough.

According to Roberts, that's what Ohtani communicated.

"He was adamant that he can help us," Roberts said. "He's well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that's all I needed to hear. I've never wavered in my belief in him."

Ohtani has not homered since Aug. 18 and has driven in only one run since. He went 11-for-70 with 29 strikeouts to finish the regular season, accumulating only three extra-base hits in the process, and has since gone 3-for-20 in the playoffs. The low point seemingly occurred in Monday's sixth inning, in an at-bat that began with Ohtani flashing bunt and ended with him flailing helplessly at a sweeper well out of the zone, losing his bat in the process.

Roberts acknowledged that Ohtani was still bothered by the left knee and right arm issues that prevented him from pitching beyond early July and eventually crept into his offense. But Ohtani, speaking through an interpreter, said his symptoms have "subdued a lot" since spending two weeks on the injured list last month.

"The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit," Ohtani said, "and even if the injuries happen by accident, I take full responsibility. I take that as an opportunity for me to just take full responsibility for it. Today it's going to be another process for me to tinker and try new things."

Ohtani began to platoon with Mookie Betts in the leadoff spot upon being activated off the IL on Sept. 23, with only five regular-season games left, and was moved back to fourth and fifth in the lineup beginning with Game 3 of the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. Against Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser in Wednesday's Game 3, Roberts said Ohtani would hit anywhere between second and sixth.

When asked whether his injuries have affected his mechanics, Ohtani said: "The results, take full responsibility. That's all I can really say, why the results haven't been where I wanted it to be. But I think there's different approaches to this, whether that be focusing on reducing the symptoms and getting rid of the pain and/or just making sure that I'm moving well in the swing."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Tuesday, Oct. 13
Blues land gun Giant

Lachie Whitfield's move to Carlton is official, with the 32-year-old joining the Blues on a three-year deal. Whitfield has played 278 games, and joins Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, and Jake Stringer in departing the Giants.

Carlton receive picks 31 and 50 along with the veteran, with pick 25, pick 26, and a 2028 third-round pick going back the other way.

Former top-five pick on the move

Zane Duursma has got his wish, joining Melbourne along with pick 52. The Roos get pick 33 and 49 in return.

Blues ruck crosses to Collingwood

Flynn Riley has been traded to the Magpies after joining Carlton in the mid-season draft this year, making his AFL debut in Round 18.

A 2028 third-round pick goes the Blues' way.

Swans trade star defender to North Melbourne

The biggest name left on the AFL trade board has tumbled, with Sydney agreeing to move Nick Blakey to North Melbourne.

The Swans offloaded Blakey, draft pick No.52 and their 2028 second-round selection in exchange for a glut of picks.

The Kangaroos traded picks No.6 and No.47, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Saints owner Gayle Benson rips 1-4 start, says fans 'deserve better'
stories.summary: Saints owner Gayle Benson called out several members of the organization amid the team's 1-4 start and said that fans are "right to expect more than we have delivered."
stories.body:
In a rare public criticism of her team, owner Gayle Benson said the Saints' 1-4 start was "not acceptable" and vowed to deliver better results to New Orleans fans.

Benson, speaking to the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club on Tuesday, said she has heard the frustration from fans "very loudly" after a three-game losing streak, saying she expects better and the fans "deserve better."

"Our fans invest their time and their hearts in the Saints," Benson said. "They are right to expect more than we have delivered."

Benson called out several members of the organization and said the responsibility starts with her as an owner. She said she will not make excuses or "accept this level of performance as our standard."

"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution."

The Saints are 7-15 since Moore took over before the 2025 season. Loomis, who has been the Saints' general manager since 2002, has not seen the team go to the playoffs since the Sean Payton/Drew Brees era in 2020.

Benson specifically called out the Week 4 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on "Monday Night Football," noting it was "truly disappointing" to lose on a night intended to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the return to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. She also spoke about honoring Brees at halftime of a loss to the Minnesota Vikings last week and said the "best way to honor that legacy is to uphold [his] standards today."

"Words will not restore our fans' confidence," Benson said. "Our performance must do that."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Chelsea confident in January move for Scott
stories.summary: Chelsea are growing confident of signing Bournemouth's Alex Scott. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Chelsea are growing confident they will be able to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott in January. Meanwhile, Barcelona and Real Madrid were at Anfield on Sunday to watch Erling Haaland when Manchester City faced Liverpool.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are increasingly confident that they will sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott during the January transfer window, according to TEAMtalk. The belief is that the 23-year-old would find it difficult to turn down a move to Stamford Bridge and the Blues are willing to meet the Cherries' demands, with any deal likely to reach around £100 million. Bournemouth turned down all interest in Scott during the summer, but the England international's contract expires in 2028 and he has so far resisted any calls for an extension.

- Barcelona and Real Madrid scouts were at Anfield to scout Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as he opened the scoring in a 3-0 win over Liverpool, according to TEAMtalk. Both of the Spanish giants continue to monitor the possibility of a future move following the club's guilty verdict for hundreds of financial charges. The two clubs weren't just there to watch City players, though: Barça have also been monitoring the situation of defender Ronald Araújo, who is on loan at Liverpool, while Madrid have been checking on Liverpool midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz.

- Borussia Dortmund have been interested in U.S. youth international and Philadelphia Union striker Malik Jakupovic for some time, reports Sky Germany. In the summer, the Bundesliga club submitted an offer for the 17-year-old that was worth €2m-€3m but was ultimately rejected. Contact continues to exist but there is major competition for Jakupovic with Chelsea, RB Salzburg and Stuttgart all looking at him while Eintracht Frankfurt also have in the past.

- Chelsea will need at least £50 million to tempt Barcelona into letting midfielder Frenkie de Jong leave in the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. Chelsea are looking at the 29-year-old as they continue their efforts to replace Enzo Fernández after the Argentina international joined Manchester City in the summer. De Jong is out injured but the Dutch midfield is nearing a return to fitness, although that return could make a move more difficult for the Blues as Barça have been eagerly awaiting his return.

- Ruben Amorim wants AC Milan to sign Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola, who has also received interest from Roma and Juventus, reports Calciomercato. Amorim was surprised by the 18-year-old's quality when the Rossoneri drew 1-1 against Sassuolo at Mapei Stadium, when Bakola was named man of the match. The young Frenchman is being considered by scouts across Europe, and having been signed for €10 million plus €2 million in add-ons last January, he could now command over €30 million.

Done deals
- Former Real Madrid right back Dani Carvajal has joined LaLiga side Getafe on a free transfer.

Other
- Arsenal are keeping an eye on Michael Olise's contract talks with Bayern Munich as they continue to look at wingers. (FootballTransfers)

- Arsenal are yet to make a decision about Max Dowman's future amid interest in a loan from Celtic and Rangers. (Football Insider)

- Several major clubs are interested in a January move for Palmeiras right back Agustin Giay, with Atletico Madrid, AC Milan and Napoli having previously made approaches. (Matteo Moretto)

- Brighton & Hove Albion see RB Salzburg midfielder Bartosz Mazurek as a leading option for January, but they face competition from Benfica and Porto. (TEAMtalk)

- Borussia Dortmund have the right to match any offer for Monaco striker Paris Brunner. (Patrick Berger)

- Napoli have started to show an interest in Union Berlin winger Livan Burcu, who is also attracting attention from other top European clubs. (Rudy Galetti)

- Borrusia Dortmund remain interested in Zaglebie Lubin attacking midfielder Marcel Rugela, but a summer move for the 19-year-old is more likely than one in January. (Patrick Berger)

- Lazio have their eyes on 18-year-old winger Filippo Toscano from Serie D side Reggina as they look to the future. (Nicolo Schira)

- Johan Bakayoko is a possible candidate to leave RB Leipzig in January despite only joining the Bundesliga club last year. (Philipp Hinze)

- AC Milan are working for a way to offload 23-year-old midfielder Warren Bondo in January. (Nicolo Schira)

stories.headline: St. Louis unbeaten run up to 20 games, tying Red Bulls' MLS record
stories.summary: Carlo Holse's hat trick helped St. Louis City SC beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games.
stories.body:
ST. LOUIS -- Carlo Holse's hat trick in the first 21 minutes -- the second hat trick in club history -- helped St. Louis City beat the LA Galaxy 6-2 on Sunday night to extend their unbeaten streak across all competitions to 20 games and tie the MLS record.

St. Louis, which is 13-0-5 in its last 18 regular-season games, tied the mark set when the New York Red Bulls went unbeaten in an MLS-record 20 consecutive games across all competitions in 2016.

Rafael Navarro converted from the penalty spot in the 45th minute, scored again in the 53rd and added two assists for St. Louis (14-6-8). Lukas MacNaughton scored on a diving header in the seventh minute of first-half stoppage time and Roman Bürki had five saves.

Holse opened the scoring in the second minute, added a goal in the seventh and skipped a shot inside the right post from the center of the area to make it 3-0 in the 21st minute to record the second-fastest hat trick in MLS history. Hany Mukhtar scored three goals for Nashville in the first 16 minutes of 5-1 win over Chicago on July 17, 2021.

The Galaxy's Kyōgo Furuhashi went off due to an apparent hamstring injury and was replaced in the 10th minute by João Klauss, whose goal in the 71st minute capped the scoring. Klauss, a 29-year-old midfielder in his first season with the Galaxy, had St. Louis City's first hat trick in a 3-3 tie with the Galaxy on June 14, 2025.

Robert Taylor scored in the 31st minute for the Galaxy (9-11-9).

St. Louis beat the Galaxy 3-1 on July 22 at Dignity Health Sports Park and hosts the Vancouver Whitecaps on Wednesday in a Western Conference top-of-table clash.

The Galaxy, who are clinging to the last playoff spot in the West, play the Portland Timbers at Dignity Health Sports Park on Wednesday. The Timbers are three points behind the Galaxy for ninth place -- the final playoff spot.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Formula 1 to return to Africa in 'early 2030s' as Rwanda race confirmed
stories.summary: Formula 1 is set to return to the African continent for the first time since 1993 after the sport confirmed a ten-year deal to host a race in Rwanda from "the early 2030s."
stories.body:
Formula 1 is set to return to the African continent for the first time since 1993 after the sport confirmed a 10-year deal to host a race in Rwanda from "the early 2030s."

After years of speculation about a return to the continent, F1 announced its plans for the "African Grand Prix" in a statement with Rwanda's president Paul Kagame on Tuesday.

The precise starting date of the new contract was not specified and is reliant on the construction of a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, 40 kilometres south of Rwanda's capital Kigali, which is set to be completed "early in the next decade."

The track, which will be built adjacent to the new Kigali International Airport, will be developed to the FIA Grade 1 standards required for F1 racing.

The last F1 race on the continent took place in South Africa in 1993 on the Kyalami circuit near Johannesburg, and Kagame described the sport's arrival in Rwanda as a moment that "belongs to Africa."

"For more than three decades, the world's premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement," Kagame said.

"Rwanda is proud to host the Formula 1 African Grand Prix, and to share this moment with more than 100 million fans across Africa, many of them young people who deserve to see the sport at home and to see themselves in it: as engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs and, one day, drivers.

"This ten-year partnership is also an investment in Rwanda's future. The circuit in Bugesera, alongside the new international airport, will bring jobs, skills, tourism and new business to our country and our region for decades to come, because our aim was never a single race weekend, but a lasting benefit for our people."

F1's statement said the new circuit would "will be designed to work in harmony with the natural landscape, using the area's elevation changes to create a unique and challenging racing experience while delivering exceptional viewing opportunities for fans."

It confirmed the circuit would be used for other international motorsport events during the rest of the year.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali, who has long held an ambition for the sport to return to F1, said: "Today is a landmark moment for Formula 1. With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the World Championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.

"Africa has always been part of Formula 1's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact.

"I would like to thank His Excellency Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda, the Government of Rwanda, the Rwanda Development Board, FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem and everyone whose dedication and collaboration have made this possible."

As recently as last weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton spoke of the importance of F1 returning to Africa in the coming years.

- Rwanda F1 race: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen welcome prospect

"I've always said that we need to have a Grand Prix in Africa," Hamilton said. "It is, for me, the most important continent and the most beautiful continent. We're on all the other continents but that one and there should be no reason for it.

"It's something I've been pushing for in the background and Stefano's been amazing -- he's flown to Africa so many times over the last couple of years speaking to lots of different people and so I hope he has some news for me soon."

The grand prix in Rwanda will be added to an already packed F1 calendar, which is currently maxed out with the sport's self-imposed limit of 24 rounds per season.

Races in Portugal and Türkiye's are set to return to the schedule next year, following on from the addition of a new venue in Madrid this year.

stories.headline: New Zealand Rugby launches legal action against ARLC over 'Chiefs' name
stories.summary: The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.
stories.body:
The battle over the use of the "Chiefs" name is headed to the New Zealand High Court after New Zealand Rugby launched legal action against the Australian Rugby League Commission.

NZR on Thursday said it had been left with no choice but to launch legal proceedings against the ARLC, who has sought to adopt the name for its Papua New Guinea expansion franchise.

The PNG Chiefs are due to join the NRL in 2028 and have already signed a raft of players, including code-hoppers Zac Lomaz and Joey Manu, but they may yet have to undergo a chanGe of name if NZR gets its way.

The Chiefs' Super Rugby franchise has existed since 1996, with NZR claiming the introduction of the PNG Chiefs would result in "significant confusion and damage" should they be allowed to compete under the name from 2028.

"New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today moved to protect the Chiefs brand and is filing proceedings in the High Court of New Zealand against the decision by the Australian Rugby League Commission (ARLC) to launch a new NRL side using "Chiefs" in its name," an NZR statement read.  

"NZR is seeking both an interim and final injunction which stops the use of the names 'PNG Chiefs', 'Chiefs' or any other similar names in New Zealand.   

"The Chiefs have competed as a professional rugby team in Super Rugby since 1996 and over those 30 years, have built a strong identity and fanbase across New Zealand, Australia and internationally.  

"In New Zealand, NZR owns both the trademark rights for the word Chiefs and the Chiefs logo and since 1998, NZR has also held trademark protection for the Chiefs logo in Australia."

NZR claims it had tried to engage with the ARLC in an attempt to find a resolution, yet the commission was now intent on proceeding with the official launch of the PNG Chiefs on Oct. 21.

"For 30 years the Chiefs and their players have built an incredibly strong identity that is widely recognised and loved by fans," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said. "We have raised our concerns with the ARLC directly and consistently over the last year in attempting to find a resolution. We now have a responsibility to protect the Chiefs brand.   

"We want to be absolutely clear, this is not about rugby league's growth in the Pacific. We welcome the development of the Pacific region through sport and the passion that the people of Papua New Guinea have for both rugby and rugby league."  

The Chiefs won two Super Rugby titles in back-to-back seasons in 2012 and 2013, and were runners-up in Super Rugby Pacific this season after suffering a crushing defeat by the Hurricanes in the decider.

The Hamilton-based team has produced countless All Blacks since its inception, with Saturday's run-on team to face the Wallabies featuring six players from the franchise.

"Here in New Zealand, when people hear 'the Chiefs', they think of this club and this region. The identity carries significant cultural meaning and connection to the region and its people, we know it means a great deal to our players and coaches past and present, fans and supporters here and around the world," Chiefs CEO Simon Graafhuis said.   

"Teams in different sports and markets can exist alongside one another with the same name, but the issue here is the similarity of our sports competing in the same market, for the same fans, in overlapping windows."  

However, ARLC executive chairman Peter V'Landys later issued a stinging rebuke, insisting he would vigorously defend PNG's right to use the Chiefs as its team name.

"The hypocrisy is mind-blowing, considering the Auckland Blues in 1996 used the NSW Blues name without any consultation or approval. The NSW Blues had been the Blues for in excess of 50 years before that," he said.

"Rugby union is obviously feeling threatened by rugby league in New Zealand, with sell-outs at most rugby league games."

No date has yet been slated for the hearing in New Zealand's High Court.
